idea.title: The E2E test passed but broke the next test
idea.summary: A password-reset E2E test changed a shared seeded account and left the database in a different state. Restoring the seed password in Playwright cleanup made the suite deterministic, including when an assertion fails.

context.goal: Keep authentication E2E tests independent and repeatable.
context.situation: The password-reset scenario uses the common seeded organization owner.
context.problem: It changed the owner's password without restoring it, so later tests could inherit invalid credentials.
context.investigation: A regression test showed the original seeded password was unavailable after the reset flow.
context.decision: Restore the seeded password in test.afterEach so cleanup runs after both passing and failing assertions.
context.implementation: Request a new reset token and confirm the known seeded password during Playwright teardown.
context.result: The full local E2E suite passed five tests, including the regression check for the original seeded password.

learning_points: A passing test can still corrupt shared E2E state.
Cleanup must run after assertion failures, not only on the happy path.
A regression test should prove the seeded baseline remains usable.
story_points: The failure was not inside password reset itself but in the state it left behind.
The fix reused the existing reset workflow rather than adding direct database mutation.
possible_angles: Why E2E tests can pass individually and fail as a suite.
The most important assertion is sometimes about cleanup, not the feature under test.
